answer: Yes. The story uses sophisticated metaphors to connect the narrator’s need for recognition with her eventual self-understanding. Martin “borrowed other people’s attention until he felt full” captures his emotional dependence, while learning painful truths “the way you learn a dark room by walking into the furniture” makes discovery feel incremental and bruising. Bread becomes a sustained symbol of existence independent of an audience. Simone Weil’s philosophy also deepens the central theme: attention develops from something the narrator craves into something she learns to give.
